transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-05 11:00 PT / Duration ~62m / Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan, Maya, Luis (HarborLane)

Summary: quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranker to improve search relevance for freight tracking docs and carrier help centre. Cover demo of endpoint calls, Redwood Console relevance insights, and Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/caching and model choice. Agreed next steps: pilot data export, benchmark script, security docs + pricing.

Topics: scope of problem, current stack (Elastic + custom BM25), target latency and cost, data residency/SOC2, demo run with sample queries, evaluation metrics (MRR, top-1 accuracy), pilot logistics.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we should be all set. i'm jordan meyers from redwood, account exec. priya is our solutions engineer, she'll do the deep dive. quick intros?
00:12 Evan: yeah evan cho here, head of search at harborlane, we own customer-facing search and internal kb. maya, luis with me.
00:18 Maya: hi! maya patel, ml eng, i work on retrieval and ranking pipelines.
00:24 Luis: luis ramirez, platform ops, i manage infra and compliance.
00:28 Jordan: awesome. goal for today is to show how our hosted API for embeddings + rerank could slot into your stack and run a short demo with your sample docs. also hit on security and pilot steps. sound right?
00:36 Evan: yep that's perfect, thanks.

01:05 Priya: quick context — i've looked at the notes you sent: you're on elastic for indexing, BM25 for initial recall, then a lightweight ranker. you want to reduce false positives for support article search and speed up self-serve. main constraints: latency under 300ms for web UI, budget conscious, and SOC2 plus EU data residency for some customers.
01:35 Maya: correct, some of our enterprise customers insist on EU-only data handling.
01:40 Priya: makes sense. hosted api can help — you can route EU traffic to our europe region, and we offer a private deployment option later if you need VPC/on-prem. for today we'll demo hosted.
02:10 Jordan: to be clear we usually recommend a two-phase approach: embeddings for semantic recall then a reranker model to rescore top-K candidates (we commonly do top-50->top-5). the hosted api exposes both endpoints.

02:40 Priya: demo plan: 1) show embeddings endpoint with their doc corp and queries, 2) show reranker endpoint that takes context + candidate docs and returns scores + excerpts, 3) show Console insights and Optimize suggestions.

03:05 Priya (screen share): ok i'm hitting POST /v1/embeddings with a sample freight doc. note — our client SDK and curl examples are in the quickstart. you'll see returned vector length 1536 (chose a mid-size model) — keep in mind models and dims vary.
03:28 Evan: is the embeddings call sync? we need to batch thousands of docs for initial ingest.
03:34 Priya: yes you can batch on the client side, also our ingest endpoints accept bulk uploads. for online queries we recommend smaller batches; for offline indexing we do bulk upserts. Optimize will suggest batch sizes based on token distribution.

04:05 Priya: now i'll run a sample query: POST /v1/search/embeddings?top_k=50 with the user query "how to update pickup address" — returns nearest neighbor ids. you'll notice re-ranking then calls POST /v1/rerank with the query plus the top candidates. reranker returns scores and highlighted spans.
04:38 Maya: what model is the reranker using?
04:40 Priya: currently using a tuned cross-encoder variant we ship in hosted. in the Console you can pick model tier — low-latency vs high-quality; we also show expected latency and cost per 1k calls. for your UI target of 300ms we recommended the low-latency reranker with prefix caching on common queries.

05:10 Luis: prefix caching — how persistent is that? encryption? we need KMS integration.
05:16 Priya: good question. cache is a prefix/KV cache — sorry the transcription sometimes writes key-value cash — it persists per-deployment and can be encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS in our Private option; for hosted we use our managed KMS but we support bring-your-own keys for Dedicated and Private.

06:00 Evan: what about throughput? our UI has spikes during morning loads, want burst capacity.
06:05 Jordan: Dedicated can give you reserved throughput and burst policies. hosted has autoscaling but with soft limits; we'll show quotas in the Console and you can request higher capacity. for pilot we usually start hosted to validate quality then move to dedicated if throughput/cost warrants.

06:45 Priya (running more queries): here's a “bad” example from your sample: query 'where is my container' — initial recall returns doc about invoice, reranker correctly demotes invoice and promotes tracking doc. you can see scores: 0.12, 0.87 etc. note transcription sometimes mixes numbers.
07:20 Maya: nice. what's the evaluation workflow? we want to track regressions.
07:26 Priya: Console has per-route relevance dashboards; you can upload labeled prompt sets for Continuous Evals. we alert when top-1 accuracy drops below threshold. Optimize suggests quantization or model switches if cost balloons but quality remains acceptable.

08:10 Evan: any concerns about PII in logs? we need audit logs and retention controls.
08:15 Priya: hosted API log policy is configurable — you can disable request logging, or redact sensitive fields. audit logs and role-based access are in the Console. we'll share the security whitepaper with SOC2, ISO certs and data retention options.

09:05 Priya: now a quick walkthrough of Console metrics — latency heatmaps, token cost by route, per-model counters. here's a per-route view for search.rerank where you can see the median p50 and 95 latencies. you can set SLO alerts and automatic fallback to smaller model when latency spikes.
09:45 Luis: fallback behavior — what about consistency? if fallback triggers, will outputs change dramatically?
09:50 Priya: fallback is to a compatible model variant; in Console you can define fallback tiers. for rerankers we recommend a smaller cross-encoder that preserves rank stability. we also support A/B rollouts and can route a % of traffic for canary testing.

11:00 Priya: switching gears to cost — embeddings dense vectors cost per 1k units, rerank is per-candidate-scored. Optimize suggests reducing top-K where costs are high and using a lightweight static filter pre-rank. we can run a cost simulation if you provide query distribution.
11:35 Evan: we'll share logs. can you run a quick sim for our traffic profile?
11:38 Priya: yes that's one of our action items — we'll run a benchmark script against your log and return expected per-month cost and latency.

13:00 Priya (demo note): small transcription glitch — sometimes firewall/proxy names get mangled. during private deployments we do customer-managed control plane and private network peering.

14:20 Maya: technical question: do you expose KV cache controls via the API or only in Console?
14:25 Priya: both — you can set cache hints in the request header and configure policies in Console. for example serve-cache: ttl=600, key=prefix(query) — sorry again the transcribed header looked like server cache.

16:00 Evan: security checklist — SSO, SAML, audit logs, SOC2, KMS, EU residency. can you map these to a timeline for pilot?
16:08 Jordan: yes, we typically provide the security pack up front. for EU residency we can ensure data routing to our EU region for hosted pilot; Private deployment for strict guarantees takes a little longer (~6-8 weeks depending on infra).

18:00 Maya: one more: latency budget from client to reranker — any recommendations for client-side retry/backoff?
18:06 Priya: we recommend optimistic client timeouts ~350ms for UI, fallback to a cached static answer if reranker times out. our SDKs have built-in retry/backoff and recorded metrics.

20:00 Priya: demo deeper dive — i'll run the rerank endpoint with a slightly adversarial example to show robustness. (runs) you can see the response includes per-candidate token offsets and a confidence score. sometimes the transcript on this bit will wrap lines oddly — apologies.

24:30 Evan: what's the turnaround to get an initial benchmark?
24:32 Jordan: we can start as soon as you provide a 2-week sample query log and 200 labeled examples for accuracy baseline. we usually turn around a bench within 3-5 business days.
24:45 Luis: any network requirements? we need CIDR ranges for firewall rules.
24:50 Jordan: we'll send the hosted API ingress IP ranges; for Private we'll discuss VPC peering.

28:10 Priya: quick note on model selection: for search rerank we often try 1) a distilled cross-encoder for sub-300ms, 2) a higher-quality cross-encoder for offline scoring. Optimize will show estimated token counts and recommended quantization for dedicated hardware.

31:00 Maya: can you surface examples where quantization impacted quality?
31:05 Priya: yes we have an examples repo. quantization can slightly degrade fine-grained answer extraction — Console's eval helps you measure that. we'll include a short case study in the follow-up.

34:20 Evan: competitors — some of our folks asked about using Pinecone + open model reranker. how do you compare?
34:28 Jordan: Pinecone is great for vector storage; Redwood offers unified serving for embeddings + rerank plus built-in reranker models and fallbacks, which reduces integration complexity. also we provide accuracy monitoring and cost tooling out of the box.

36:00 Priya: bringing it together — pilot proposal: 2-week hosted pilot, we run benchmark on your logs, tune top-K and reranker model, provide Console access and a small dashboard for relevance metrics. two Good success criteria: top-1 accuracy improves by X% (we'll agree baseline) and median latency <300ms for UI queries.

38:00 Evan: sounds good. timeline?
38:05 Jordan: if you send logs by 2027-10-11 we can start benchmark and have results by 2027-10-18. contract/pilot pricing doc by 2027-10-08.

40:00 Maya: any limitations we should be aware of up front?
40:05 Priya: hosted won't give you a contract-backed physical network isolation — that's Dedicated/Private. also extremely large offline corp ingest may need batching and sharded writes, but we have bulk ingest docs. Sometimes the ASR stutters on model names (e.g., cross-encoder vs cross encoder).

42:00 Jordan: recap of next steps — we'll send pricing/contract one-pager, security whitepaper link, and a benchmark plan. priya will prepare a benchmark script and run with your logs. evan will supply logs and labeled examples. luis will get firewall/CIDR requirements.

42:30 Evan: perfect. any other questions from HarborLane?
42:35 Maya: no, thanks this was thorough.
42:38 Luis: no, looks good.

43:00 Jordan: cool thanks everyone — i'll email the artifact links: quickstart repo, security whitepaper, and pilot pricing. links mentioned in call: https://redwood.example.com/quickstart, https://redwood.example.com/security.pdf, demo notebook gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/harborlane-demo.

44:00 Priya: one last note — if we hit quality regressions during pilot we can enable canary rollouts and automatic fallback, and tie alerts to your incident slack channel.

45:30 Evan: okay let's do it. thanks.

Final Recap: 1) HarborLane to send 2-week query logs + 200 labeled examples by 2027-10-11 2) Redwood to deliver benchmark results and pilot cost projection by 2027-10-18 3) Redwood to send contract and pilot pricing by 2027-10-08 4) Setup Console access for Evan/Maya during pilot

Action items (repeat inside transcript): Priya to run benchmark script; Evan to export logs; Jordan to send pricing and security docs.

End of transcript.
